name: Shook Ones
label: Revelation
lede: A Bellingham melodic hardcore band that sold its first Revelation covers at a basement show in Ballard, lost jobs and phone service to a European tour, and came back to the label a decade later sounding like a band with nothing to prove.

eras.title: From the Velvet Elvis to Bellingham
eras.text: Scott Freeman grew up going to all-ages shows in Seattle at the Velvet Elvis, RKCNDY and DV8. By 2004 he had a band in Bellingham, a demo, and fast, tuneful hardcore that caught Revelation's ear within two years.

years.h: Scott Freeman starts Shook Ones in Bellingham, Washington
years.p: After laying groundwork in 2003 and 2004, singer Scott Freeman gets Shook Ones going in Bellingham. A demo comes first.
Shook Ones' first full-length comes out on Endwell Records.

eras.title: Too hands off
eras.text: Revelation gave Shook Ones two records and plenty of freedom, and the band used it to tour: the US, Japan, and almost four weeks in Europe that cost them their jobs. By late 2007 they had left the label.

years.h: Slaughter of the Insole tour covers end up at a Ballard basement show
years.p: Shook Ones' first Revelation 7" was meant to ship with 60 special tour covers. After delays, Revelation says, those became release-show covers, sold at a basement show in Ballard.
years.xp: The first press was 300 on pink and 700 on purple, and the 7" was repressed on white and, in 2012, on green.

years.src: Scene Point Blank · Revelation Records pressing history
years.h: Facetious Folly Feat, recorded and mixed in four days · REV 142
years.p: Shook Ones' second album, and only full-length on Revelation, was tracked and mixed in four days. The first press came in yellow/brown split, red/yellow sunburst and red.
Shook Ones play Japan in April 2007. They also release a split with the Japanese band Easel in these years.

years.h: A Shook Ones European tour costs jobs and phone service
years.p: On a Shook Ones European tour of nearly four weeks, band members lose their jobs back home and have their cell phones cut off for lack of money, Scott Freeman told Redefine.

q: hands off, but almost too hands off
years.p: Shook Ones part ways with Revelation, one of several bands to leave the label between 2005 and 2007. Scott Freeman says Revelation never did anything shady, but its money went to mail order first.

Shook Ones' third album comes out on Paper + Plastick, run by [[Less Than Jake|e54e065f-0ce6-4779-9a9a-afd7b997471f]] drummer Vinnie Fiorello, after a 2008 split with End of a Year on Runner Up. Twelve days in the studio this time.
years.xp: Scott Freeman said Fiorello's label put almost no creative limits on the band. Their split-EP song Order Form is about gay rights.

eras.title: Almost a decade later
eras.text: Shook Ones never announced a breakup. They put out a few singles in 2013, then spent more than a year making a record with every member writing, and brought it back to Revelation.

years.h: Shook Ones put out new singles
years.p: Shook Ones release a few singles, their last new music for five years.

years.h: Shook Ones start tracking Body Feel on the Fourth of July
years.p: Recording starts at Hear Me Shimmer and the Loom Room. Everyone writes, including members who don't play guitar writing guitar parts.

years.src: No Echo · Revelation Records pressing history
years.h: Body Feel: Shook Ones back on Revelation · REV 176
years.p: Shook Ones' first album in nearly a decade, mixed and mastered by Jack Shirley at Atomic Garden. No Echo premiered Night Blind.
Shook Ones play a hometown release show for Body Feel in Bellingham, Washington.
